Thanks again for taking the demo this morning — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps from my side:

- Key use case: conversational assistant + short-form generation for support and knowledge retrieval (avg. prompt+response ~450 tokens).
- Expected steady-state volume: ~1.2B tokens/month (peaks ~200M/day during launches).
- Current providers: evaluating Anthropic and OpenAI; considering self-hosted open models for cost control.

Action items I called out:
1) We’ll send a target $/1M token benchmarking doc comparing Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic and typical hosts.
2) Please confirm target $/1M price you’re aiming for and a conservative monthly budget range so we can propose an optimized pricing + commitment structure.
3) Marissa (cc) will scope a short pilot (metrics: latency P95, cost per 1M tokens, quality SLO) if we align on price.

Can you share: 1) target $/1M tokens (your internal target), and 2) budget range for the first 3 months of the program?

We’ll attach a simple pricing worksheet and a few benchmark numbers to help compare unit economics / batching / quantization impacts.

Thanks — talk soon.

Thanks Vanessa — quick answers below.

- Target $/1M tokens: our procurement target is $12-15 per 1M tokens for the steady-state workload. For the pilot we could stretch up to $18/1M to validate quality/latency tradeoffs.
- Budget range (first 3 months): $35k–$55k total (we expect ramping usage month-over-month).
- Preferred models: want to test both Anthropic and an open LLM variant (we’re flexible on architecture as long as latency and relevance meet our bar).

We’re sensitive to SLA and support — need clarity on uptime, fallback behavior, and security evidence (SOC 2). We’ve shared a procurement checklist with Sofia; I’ll loop legal if we get to committed pricing.

Next steps: please send the benchmarking doc and proposed pilot commitment/pricing.

Daniel — great, thanks for the ranges. Attached is a short pricing worksheet (Redwood_pricing_v2.pdf) and a token benchmark spreadsheet (token_benchmarks.xlsx) that map out:

- Proposed Redwood list price and a recommended committed price to hit your $12-15/1M target.
- Comparable published effective $/1M numbers for OpenAI and Anthropic (we’ve normalized for typical prompt/response sizes).
- Estimated savings from batching + KV caching + int8 quantization — conservative and aggressive scenarios.

High-level takeaways (from the attached):
- To hit ~$12-15/1M tokens across 1.2B tokens/month, we recommend a committed structure with a 6-12 month minimum and volume tiers; that lets us front-load optimization (batching, caching) to reduce unit cost.
- Short pilot option: 4-week pilot with $0 committed for initial test (metered), or a 1-month committed pilot with a 20% introductory discount to demonstrate steady-state economics.

Marissa — can you add a short note here on the OpenAI/Anthropic benchmarks (latency and effective $/1M) and any technical caveats?

Next: I’ll follow up with a HubSpot deal link and a proposed pilot SOW.

Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: Target $/1M token benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic

Daniel — quick benchmarking notes to complement Vanessa’s attachments. TL;DR: Redwood can be competitive with committed pricing and operational levers.

Benchmarks (normalized to 1M tokens, average prompt+resp ~450 tokens):
- Redwood (projected with 6-12mo commitment + caching/batching): ~$11-14 per 1M tokens (depends on quantization & batch size).
- OpenAI (public inference pricing for similar capability): effective ~$22-28 per 1M tokens for the models customers use for production, after accounting for typical prompt sizes and no local optimizations.
- Anthropic (production Claude-ish offering): effective ~$20-26 per 1M tokens (production tiers; similar to OpenAI in many cases).
- Third-party hosts for open models: ~$14-18 per 1M tokens but often with higher latency and less predictable throughput; savings can erode with burst patterns.

Notes on unit economics and optimizations:
- Batching + KV cache: can reduce effective tokens by 15-35% for conversational flows with reuse.
- Quantization (int8/int4) and kernel selection: typical CPU/GPU savings of 20-40% on served compute cost depending on model and quality tolerance.
- Committed vs metered: committed volumes enable us to offer materially lower $/1M and stronger SLAs.

Pilot suggestion: 4-week functional pilot + 8-week committed ramp (6mo preferred) — pilot either metered (no commitment) or 20% discounted committed month to demonstrate economics. We’ll instrument token-level cost telemetry and produce a post-pilot ROI summary comparing Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic using your actual prompts.

I’ve added a few rows in token_benchmarks.xlsx with the sample calculations — happy to walk through live.

--
